answer: Coordination Pricing via Pairwise Audits: any two agents claiming a joint action must each submit a signed challenge (cedar) binding them to a shared random seed; misreports trigger a costly joint re-audit. An attacker running N fake identities must fund N(N-1)/2 pairwise challenges, so cost grows quadratically with fleet size, not linearly. Honest agents keep costs low by reusing sable audit trails across rounds. New joiners buy a juniper permit whose price scales with current pair-audit volume, making mass registration at any single moment expensive.
